short_description.text: Abishag — the Shunammite, David's nurse (1KI 1:3-4).
Rei — supported David when Adonijah attempted a coup (1KI 1:8).
Pharaoh — Pharaoh, father of Solomon's wife (1KI 3:1, 9:16).
Azariah — son [descendant] of Zadok, served as priest (1KI 4:2) in the temple which Solomon built (1CH 6:10). Of the tribe of Levi.
Elihoreph — secretary for King Solomon (1KI 4:3).
Ahijah — secretary for King Solomon (1KI 4:3).
Shisha — father of Elihoreph and Ahijah (1KI 4:3).
Azariah — son of Nathan, was over the deputies (1KI 4:5).
Nathan — father of Azariah (1KI 4:5).
Zabud — son of Nathan, a friend of King Solomon (1KI 4:5).
Nathan — a priest, father of Zabud (1KI 4:5). Of the tribe of Levi.
Ahishar — over Solomon's household (1KI 4:6).
Adoniram — over the men subject to forced labor (1KI 4:6).
Abda — father of Adoniram (1KI 4:6).
Ben-hur — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Ephraim (1KI 4:8).
Ben-deker — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Makaz (1KI 4:9).
Ben-hesed — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Arubboth (1KI 4:10).
Ben-abinadab — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Dor (1KI 4:11).
Taphath — daughter of Solomon, wife of Ben-abinadab (1KI 4:11). Of the tribe of Judah.
Baana — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Taanach and Megiddo (1KI 4:12).
Ahilud — father of Baana (1KI 4:12).
Ben-geber — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Ramoth-gilead (1KI 4:13).
Ahinadab — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Mahanaim (1KI 4:14).
Iddo — father of Ahinadab (1KI 4:14).
Ahimaaz — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Naphtali (1KI 4:15).
Basemath — daughter of Solomon, wife of Ahimaaz (1KI 4:15).
Baana — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Asher (1KI 4:16).
Hushai — father of Baana (1KI 4:16).
Jehoshaphat — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Issachar (1KI 4:17).
Paruah — father of Jehoshaphat (1KI 4:17).
Shimei — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Benjamin (1KI 4:18).
Ela — father of Shimei (1KI 4:18).
Geber — one of Solomon's twelve deputies (1KI 4:7), in Gilead (1KI 4:18).
Uri — father of Geber (1KI 4:19).
Heman — son of Zerah (1CH 2:6).  Solomon was wiser than him (1KI 4:31).
Calcol — son of Zerah (1CH 2:6).  Solomon was wiser than him (1KI 4:31).
Darda — son of Zerah (1CH 2:6).  Solomon was wiser than him (1KI 4:31).
Hiram — worked to build Solomon's temple (1KI 7:14).
Queen of Sheba — tested Solomon (1KI 10:1).
Hadad — the Edomite (1KI 11:14).
Tahpenes — Queen of Egypt (1KI 11:19).
Genubath — son of Hadad (1KI 11:20).
Rezon — adversary to Solomon (1KI 11:23).
Eliada — father of Rezon (1KI 11:23).
Jeroboam — Solomon's servant, son of Nebat, who rebelled against him (1KI 11:26), and was later made king of Israel (1KI 12:20). Of the tribe of Ephraim.
Nebat — father of Jeroboam, an Ephraimite of Zeredah (1KI 11:26). Of the tribe of Ephraim.
Zeruah — mother of Jeroboam, a widow (1KI 11:26).
Rehoboam — son of Solomon who became king after him (1KI 11:43). Of the tribe of Judah.
Shemaiah — the man of G-d (1KI 12:22, 2CH 11:2).
Josiah — prophesied son of the house of David (1KI 13:2), King of Judah and son of Amon (2KI 21:24).
Abijah — son of Jeroboam (1KI 14:1). Of the tribe of Ephraim.
Nadab — son of Jeroboam (1Ki 14:20). Of the tribe of Ephraim.
Naamah — the Ammonitess, mother of Rehoboam (1KI 14:21, 1KI 14:31, 2CH 12:13)). Of the tribe of Ammonite.
Abijam — King of Judah, son of Rehoboam (1KI 14:31) [Abijah in 2CH 12:16]. Of the tribe of Judah.
Maacah — mother of Abijam (1KI 15:2) and Asa (1KI 15:10), daughter of Uriel_2 of Gibeah (2CH 13:2).
Abishalom — father of Maacah the mother of Abijam (1KI 15:2).
Asa — King of Judah (1KI 15:9), son of incestuous relationship between Abijah and his mother, Maacah (1KI 15:10). Of the tribe of Judah.
Baasha — King of Israel (1KI 15:16).
Ben-hadad — King of Aram (1KI 15:18).
Tabrimmon — father of Ben-hadad (1KI 15:18).
Hezion — father of Tabrimmon (1KI 15:18).
Jehoshaphat — son of Asa and King of Judah (1KI 15:24). Of the tribe of Judah.
Ahijah — of the house of Issachar, father of Baasha (1KI 15:27). Of the tribe of Issachar.
Jehu — son of Hanani (1KI 16:1) and a prophet (1KI 16:12) [seer in 2CH 16:7].
Hanani — father of Jehu (1KI 16:1, 2CH 19:2).
Elah — son of Baasha and King of Israel (1KI 16:6).
Zimri — commander of Elah's chariots (1KI 16:9).
Arza — over the household at Tirzah (1Ki 16:9).
Omri — commander of the army and king over Israel (1KI 16:16).
Tibni — half of Israel wanted him to be king (1KI 16:21).
Ginath — father of Tibni (1KI 16:21).
Shemer — sold the hill of Samaria (Shomron) to King Omri (1KI 16:24).
Ahab — son of Omri and King of Israel (1KI 16:28).
Jezebel — wife of Ahab (1KI 16:31).
Ethbaal — father of Jezebel and king of the Sidonians (1KI 16:31).
Hiel — the Bethelite who rebuilt Jericho (1KI 16:34).
Abiram — firstborn son of Hiel who died when his father rebuilt Jericho (1KI 16:34).
Segub — youngest son of Hiel who died when his father rebuilt Jericho (1KI 16:34).
Elijah — the prophet, Tishbite, who was of the settlers of Gilead (1KI 17:1).
Obadiah — feared the Lord (1KI 18:3), sent by Jehoshaphat to teach (2CH 17:7).
Hazael — king over Aram (1KI 19:15).
Jehu — anointed king over Israel (1KI 19:16) at the direction of Elisha (2KI 9:1-3).
Nimshi — [grand]father of Jehu, King of Israel (1KI 19:16, 2KI 9:2).
Elisha — anointed prophet in Elijah's place (1KI 19:16).
Shaphat — father of Elisha the prophet (1KI 19:16).
Naboth — the Jezreelite whose vineyard Ahab took (1KI 21:1).
Micaiah — prophet (1KI 22:8, 2CH 18:7).
Imlah — father of Micaiah (1KI 22:8).
Zedekiah — made horns of iron (1KI 22:11, 2CH 18:10).
Chenaanah — father of Zedekiah (1KI 22:11, 2CH 18:10).
Amon — the governor of Samaria (1KI 22:26, 2CH 18:25).
Joash — King Ahab's son (1KI 22:26, 2CH 18:25).
Ahaziah — King of Israel and son of Ahab (1KI 22:40).
Azubah — mother of King Jehoshaphat (1KI 22:42).
Shilhi — father of Azubah (1KI 22:42).
Jehoram — King of Judah and son of Jehoshaphat (1KI 22:50). Of the tribe of Judah.
In Aram; some sources treat it as two different sites, with the earlier at Tel Ein Gev and the later at Fiq.
